title: Choose a real-server test for async Server Component behavior
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed tests/product.spec.ts change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode:
// A mocked React render is being presented as proof of routing, server caching and streaming correctness.
expect(mockedProduct).toEqual({id:'one'});

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Run the test against a production build.
Add missing-resource, failure and soft-navigation journeys.
Use an origin counter or controlled clock for cache claims rather than inferring them from a visible heading.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: A pure unit test is valuable for policy logic but cannot establish the framework’s async rendering, route conventions, response headers or caching.
Run the test against a production build.
alternativeApproaches: No. Test pure transformations and authorization matrices cheaply at unit level, then cover the small number of real framework and deployment boundaries with integration/E2E evidence. Mocks and real-server evidence answer different questions.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

verification: Run the test against a production build.
Add missing-resource, failure and soft-navigation journeys.
Use an origin counter or controlled clock for cache claims rather than inferring them from a visible heading.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
